lessons: STALE FIXED: the monthly-vs-bi-monthly VAT filing threshold was NIS 1,520,000; the figure in force from 1 January 2026 is NIS 1,775,000, measured over the determining year (12 consecutive months ending 31 August of the preceding tax year) rather than the calendar year. Verified against the Kol Zchut periodic-returns page.

STALE FIXED (direction error): the skill warned not to confuse the filing-frequency threshold with the detailed-reporting obligation but described the latter as kicking in at a HIGHER turnover. It is much LOWER. Added the real rule: from 1 January 2026 a self-employed individual above NIS 500,000 turnover must file the itemised PCN874 detailed report, which must reconcile exactly with the periodic return. This closes the standing carry note from cycle 1.2.0 about not conflating the two.

TENSE STALENESS FIXED: the allocation-number section presented NIS 10,000 as current and NIS 5,000 as a future step-down. The 5,000 threshold took effect 1 June 2026 on schedule (verified, not deferred), so an agent reading the skill after that date could have applied the wrong figure. Both languages now state 5,000 as in force with 10,000 as history. This is a recurring failure mode for scheduled step-downs: write the CURRENT value as the headline and relegate the schedule to context.

CLI DISCLOSURE ADDED: the skill is built entirely on the gws CLI but never disclosed that the project states it is NOT an officially supported Google product, is pre-v1.0 with expected breaking changes, and builds its command surface dynamically from Google's Discovery Service rather than a fixed list. Users now get that up front, plus the instruction to run `gws sheets --help` rather than trusting a remembered command.

INSTALL PATH FIXED: the skill gave only `npm install -g @googleworkspace/cli`. The project's recommended install is the pre-built binary from GitHub Releases; npm is a convenience wrapper around the same binary and needs Node 18+.

CRITICAL: parse_amount silently returned 0.0 for currency-formatted cells. Step 3 tells the user to format amounts as ILS currency and the Sheets API returns FORMATTED_VALUE by default, so the documented happy path produced a confident all-zero VAT report with exit 0. Now parses the shekel sign, thousands separators and parenthesised negatives, and RAISES on an unparseable non-empty cell.

CRITICAL: input VAT was summed blindly. Added the three limits the skill never mentioned: no input VAT at all on a private vehicle (Reg. 14(a), even at 100% business use), generally none on hospitality/refreshments/gifts, and 2/3 or 1/4 on mixed business/private inputs (Reg. 18). The script now flags matching rows and states explicitly that it sums rather than applies the limits. Every one of these omissions understated VAT owed.

CRITICAL: the 80% meals rate was over-generalised from the skill's own evidence snippet, which says light refreshments AT THE PLACE OF BUSINESS, into 'business meals with clients'. Hosting/entertainment is generally not deductible at all. Example 3 and the Step 8 sample row instructed the agent to make exactly that error.

CRITICAL: the car income-tax rule was inverted (the test is the HIGHER of 45% or upkeep minus shovi shimush, not the lower), and 'fixed deduction per km' was fabricated. There is no per-kilometre regime for the Israeli self-employed.

CRITICAL: added the book-of-account warning. A freely editable Google Sheet is not a kovetz kavua and fails the non-deletion, auto-sequential-numbering and additive-correction requirements, so the user needs a compliant invoicing and bookkeeping system alongside it. The skill previously said only that the sheet is not the legal invoice, then stopped.
FABRICATED DATE REMOVED: the tax calendar carried 'Jul 31 - mikdamot H1'. There is no semi-annual advance-payment deadline; advances follow a monthly (or approved bi-monthly) rhythm.

SCRIPT: Hebrew Type values (hachnasa/hotzaa) were unrecognised and silently produced a zero report; unknown types are now counted and warned about. Income and expense category totals were conflated into one list that was exported to the accountant's CSV; now split. Negative net VAT was labelled 'Liability (to pay)'; now labelled a refund claim.

SCRIPT: backup-sheets.py's per-tab `except Exception` was dead code because run_gws called sys.exit (SystemExit is not an Exception), so one bad tab killed the whole run. run_gws now raises GwsError, every tab is attempted, and the process exits non-zero if any failed. --tabs is now required rather than silently defaulting to Sheet1 while the help claimed 'all'.

CLI VERIFIED CLEAN: an independent audit installed @googleworkspace/cli and dry-ran all 64 gws invocations across every file. No fabricated subcommand, flag or argument shape. The +read/+append helpers, --dry-run and --format csv are all real. This was the biggest fabrication risk and the skill got it right.
